lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Let's go through the accounts, ferryman, if you don't mind: what you already owe me. Then we don't have to quarrel about it again later.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Let's. Better to have it settled. Less nuisance all round.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You asked me to bring an anchor. Five drachmas.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: By Hades, I paid five for it. And a rowlock: two obols.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Put down five drachmas and two obols.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And a sail-needle. Repairs for the canvas. I laid out five obols.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And wax for caulking the cracks in the little boat, and nails, and a bit of cord you made the brace out of. Two drachmas for the lot.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: That's everything—unless something has escaped us in the reckoning. So. When do you say you'll pay it back?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Right now, Hermes? Impossible. But if some plague or war sends us a crowd all at once, then I can make a margin by miscounting the ferry fares.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So I'm supposed to sit here praying for catastrophe, just so I can get reimbursed?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: There's no other way, Hermes. At the moment, as you see, hardly anyone is coming down. Peace.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Peace is better, even if it means your debt to me keeps maturing. Still—Charon, you remember what the old arrivals used to be like: brave men, all of them, most soaked in blood and full of wounds. Now it's someone poisoned by his son, or by his wife; or some soft-living fellow swollen up in belly and legs. Pale, the lot of them. No breeding. Nothing like the old ones. And most of them are here over money, apparently, plotting against each other.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Well, it is such a lovable thing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Then I don't suppose I look especially unreasonable, pressing you sharply for what you owe me.
